description.p: A GTK4 and libadwaita interface for controlling AdGuard CLI on Linux: start and stop the filtering proxy, manage filter lists, and configure protection settings without using the terminal.
This is an unofficial, community-built interface. It requires AdGuard CLI to be installed separately and is not affiliated with or endorsed by AdGuard.
First release. The whole of AdGuard CLI's day-to-day operation, without the terminal:

ul.li: Proxy status, start, stop and restart, with the licence and the proxy endpoints.
The six protection modules, and the 26 stealth settings behind them.
Filter lists from AdGuard's own catalogue, plus custom lists installed and removed by URL.
A DNS page: the DNS filter catalogue, your own rules, the servers and the listen port.
Advanced settings: proxy mode, ports, listen address, authentication, outbound proxy and logging.
A tray icon carrying start, stop and the protection toggles.
A first-run assistant for a machine where AdGuard has never been configured.
Checks for the three things AdGuard needs outside its configuration — a trusted certificate, its root helper, and browser integration — each paired with AdGuard's own command to fix it.
